title: How to Tell If a Pipe Is Leaking Behind a Wall

seo.title: How to Tell If a Pipe Is Leaking Behind a Wall

content_html:
A pipe leaking behind a wall usually creates a localized pattern: an expanding stain, soft paint or drywall, musty odor, water sound, or meter movement with no intended use. First confirm whether the damp area follows plumbing and whether it changes when a nearby fixture is used.

Relate the stain to nearby water use

Mark the edge of dampness and see whether it changes after using a shower, sink, or appliance on the same wall. A supply leak may continue without use; a drain leak more often appears while water is flowing.

Check for soft, swollen, or unusually cool material

Drywall that gives way, bubbling paint, or swollen wood indicates moisture that has been present for some time. Do not press on a heavily wet ceiling or remove material when it may fall or wiring may be behind it.

Use the meter to support a supply-line suspicion

With all use stopped, meter movement plus a stain that keeps growing increases suspicion of a pressurized supply leak. A stationary meter does not rule out a drain leak that occurs only when a fixture is used.

Shut water off for an active leak and limit wall opening

If moisture is increasing quickly, close the identified branch or main water valve and arrange repair. A small opening may be needed for drying and access, but locate plumbing and electricity first so the investigation does not create another hazard.

faq.question: How does timing help separate a supply leak from a drain leak?
faq.answer: Mark the edge of dampness and see whether it changes after using a shower, sink, or appliance on the same wall. A supply leak may continue without use; a drain leak more often appears while water is flowing.

faq.question: Which signs show that wall material is already wet?
faq.answer: Drywall that gives way, bubbling paint, or swollen wood indicates moisture that has been present for some time. Do not press on a heavily wet ceiling or remove material when it may fall or wiring may be behind it.

faq.question: What should I do if a wall stain is growing quickly?
faq.answer: If moisture is increasing quickly, close the identified branch or main water valve and arrange repair. A small opening may be needed for drying and access, but locate plumbing and electricity first so the investigation does not create another hazard.
